facts.text: Staged intervention means a collision system acts in steps of increasing force, from a quiet information signal through warnings and gentle slowing to hard braking and a locked stop, rather than jumping straight to an emergency stop.
facts.quote: Staged intervention means that a collision system acts in steps of increasing force, from a quiet information signal through warnings and gentle slowing to hard braking and a locked stop, rather than jumping straight to an emergency stop.

facts.text: The earth-moving-machine intervention ladder is assembled from standards and field evidence; each step is taken only if the operator has not reduced the risk and the stopping margin keeps shrinking.
facts.quote: each step is taken only if the operator has not reduced the risk and the stopping margin keeps shrinking.

facts.text: The information-signal stage of staged intervention provides only a visual indication when an object is present but the stopping margin is healthy.
facts.quote: *Information signal.* An object is present but the stopping margin is healthy; a visual indication only.

facts.text: The urgent-warning stage of staged intervention uses a distinct sound, light or vibration when risk is rising but the operator still has time to act.
facts.quote: *Urgent warning.* Risk is rising while the operator still has time; a distinct sound, light or vibration.

facts.text: The automatic-slowing stage reduces the drive request or uses the retarder to slow the machine smoothly when the operator does not react and stopping margin remains.
facts.quote: *Automatic slowing.* The operator does not react and margin remains; the drive request is reduced or the retarder slows the machine smoothly.

facts.text: The partial-braking stage applies controlled braking below stability and traction limits when the safe margin is approaching its minimum.
facts.quote: *Partial braking.* The safe margin is approaching its minimum; controlled braking below the limits of stability and traction.

facts.text: The maximum-safe-braking stage applies the hardest braking permitted by current stability and control limits when a collision is otherwise unavoidable.
facts.quote: *Maximum safe braking.* A collision is otherwise unavoidable; the hardest braking the current stability and control limits allow.

facts.text: No universal maximum deceleration for off-road machines was found.
facts.quote: No universal maximum deceleration for off-road machines was found.

facts.text: Stopped-state hold keeps the brake applied when the machine is at zero speed and the hazard remains; where rolling away is possible, release requires an operator action.
facts.quote: *Stopped-state hold.* The machine is at zero speed and the hazard remains; the brake is held and released only after an operator action where rolling away is possible.

facts.text: Motion inhibit from standstill rejects a move command when something is already in the machine's path, covering a start-up hazard that time to collision cannot detect.
facts.quote: *Motion inhibit from standstill.* Something is already in the path before the machine moves; the move command is rejected. This covers the start-up hazard that time to collision cannot see.

facts.text: Road AEB uses a shorter intervention sequence: warning, brief brake jerk, partial braking and full braking.
facts.quote: Road AEB uses a shorter version: warning, brief brake jerk, partial braking, full braking [Chapter 8].

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 requires distinguishable warning levels.
facts.quote: ISO 21815-3 requires distinguishable warning levels

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 places automatic action at collision-risk level 4 or above.
facts.quote: ISO 21815-3 requires distinguishable warning levels and places automatic action at collision-risk level 4 or above [Chapter 8].

facts.text: Escalation from partial to maximum braking should depend on remaining stopping margin and its uncertainty, not distance alone; visibility, target type, grade and surface conditions can make equal distances represent different risks.
facts.quote: The step from partial to maximum braking should depend on the remaining stopping margin and its uncertainty, not on distance alone

facts.text: Frequent staged-intervention signals can overload the operator.
facts.quote: Frequent signals overload the operator

facts.text: Automatic slowing may be too weak downhill.
facts.quote: slowing may be too weak downhill

facts.text: Partial braking may keep the machine in the hazard zone longer and conflict with following machines.
facts.quote: partial braking may keep the machine in the hazard zone longer and conflict with following machines

facts.text: Maximum braking risks rollover, articulation instability, load shift and sliding.
facts.quote: maximum braking risks rollover, articulation instability, load shift and sliding

facts.text: Motion inhibit disrupts close work.
facts.quote: motion inhibit disrupts close work [Chapter 8].

facts.text: Mine leaders preferred a collision system that slowed to a crawl before braking.
facts.quote: mine leaders preferred a system that slowed to a crawl before braking

facts.text: Underground workers rejected abrupt stops.
facts.quote: underground workers rejected abrupt stops [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Each intervention stage needs its own thresholds, tests and evidence, multiplying validation work.
facts.quote: Each stage needs its own thresholds, tests and evidence, which multiplies the validation work

facts.text: Staged intervention allows a first release to use gentler stages while harder interventions are still being proven.
facts.quote: lets a first release use the gentler stages while the harder ones are still being proven [Chapters 1, 8].
